questions.question: What is the primary difference between pull and push connectors in Event Management?

options.text: Pull connectors poll external tools while push connectors receive events sent to the instance
Push connectors are only available for cloud sources
Pull connectors are faster than push connectors

explanation.correct: Pull connectors actively poll external monitoring tools to retrieve events, while push connectors receive events that are sent directly to the ServiceNow instance via listeners or web service APIs. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Bandwidth usage depends on event volume, not connector type
Push connectors work with various sources, not just cloud
Speed depends on configuration and network, not connector type

source.excerpt: Event Management provides many connectors to pull or push events from external devices.

questions.question: Which two pull connectors are provided with Event Management for Microsoft environments? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: Event Management provides SCOM connector for System Center Operations Manager (versions 2007, 2012, 2016) and Azure Monitor connector for sending alert state changes to the Azure Portal. Both are pull connectors. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Microsoft Teams is not an Event Management connector
Microsoft 365 is not an Event Management connector

source.excerpt: SCOM: Alert and metric collection from the Microsoft System Center Operations Manager. Azure Monitor: Send alert state changes to the Azure Portal.

questions.question: Which connector is used to receive events from VMware vSphere environments?

explanation.correct: The vCenter connector (supported version 6.5) is used to receive events from VMware vSphere environments. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: vRealize connector is for vRealize Operations Log and Event Management
VMware ESXi connector is not a standard Event Management connector
vSphere Direct is not a standard connector name

source.excerpt: vCenter: 6.5. Receive events from your VMware vSphere environment.

questions.question: Where can Event Management connectors be obtained from?

options.text: Only from the base system installation
From the ServiceNow Store and third parties, or created as custom connectors
Only by purchasing from third-party vendors

explanation.correct: Connectors are available from the ServiceNow Store as well as from third parties. You can also create custom connectors to meet specific integration needs. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Connectors come from multiple sources, not just base system
ServiceNow Store provides many connectors, not just third parties
Connectors don't require Professional Services

source.excerpt: Connectors are available from the ServiceNow store as well as from third parties. You can also create custom connectors.

questions.question: Which two connectors require Operational Intelligence plugin (com.snc.sa.metric) to be activated before they display? (Choose two.)

explanation.correct: The Azure Metrics and AWS CloudWatch Metrics connectors display in the base system only when the Operational Intelligence plugin (com.snc.sa.metric) is activated. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: SolarWinds connector is available without Operational Intelligence plugin
Nagios connector is available without Operational Intelligence plugin

source.excerpt: The Azure Metrics and AWS CloudWatch Metrics connectors display in the base system only when the Operational Intelligence plugin (com.snc.sa.metric) is activated.

questions.question: Which feature is supported by all Event Management connectors for storing credentials?

explanation.correct: All connectors support external credential storage solutions. This allows secure management of credentials outside the ServiceNow instance. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Not all connectors use OAuth; external credential storage is universal
LDAP is one option, not the universal feature
Certificate auth is one option, not the universal feature

source.excerpt: All connectors support external credential storage solutions.

questions.question: Which connector is used to receive events from Apache Kafka?

explanation.correct: The Apache Kafka Consumer Connector (supported versions 3.0.0 and 3.2.0) is used to receive events from the Apache Kafka server. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Kafka Message Connector is not the correct name
Apache Streaming Connector is not a standard connector
Kafka Event Bridge is not a standard connector name

source.excerpt: Apache Kafka Consumer Connector: 3.0.0, 3.2.0. Receive events from the Apache Kafka server.

questions.question: An organization uses IBM for their monitoring solution. Which connector should they configure?

explanation.correct: The IBM Netcool connector (version 8.1.0) is used to receive events from IBM Netcool/OMNIbus Object Servers and Impact Servers. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: IBM Tivoli connector is not listed in standard connectors
IBM Monitoring is not a specific connector name
IBM Watson is not an Event Management connector

source.excerpt: IBM Netcool: 8.1.0. Receive events from IBM Netcool/OMNIbus Object Servers and Impact Servers.

questions.question: Which is NOT a method of sending events directly to a ServiceNow instance?

explanation.correct: Events can be sent directly to your instance via email server, script, SNMP trap, or web service API. FTP file transfer is not a standard method for sending events to Event Management. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/em-process-flow.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Email server is a valid event ingestion method
SNMP trap is a valid event ingestion method
Web service API is a valid event ingestion method

source.excerpt: Events are sent directly to your instance via email server, script, SNMP trap, or web service API.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow Cloud product has a dedicated connector for Event Management?

explanation.correct: ServiceNow Cloud Observability (version 2.1.1 or higher) has a dedicated connector to receive events from the ServiceNow Cloud Observability platform. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Cloud Discovery is not a specific connector in Event Management
Cloud Insights is not listed as a standard connector
Cloud Analytics is not a specific Event Management connector

source.excerpt: ServiceNow Cloud Observability: 2.1.1 or higher. Receive events from the ServiceNow Cloud Observability platform.

questions.question: Which push connector supports both OAuth and basic authentication for event collection?

explanation.correct: Dynatrace supports both OAuth authentication and basic authentication for event collection through the instance. Other connectors like Azure, Datadog, and ThousandEyes also support dual authentication. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Prometheus supports only basic authentication.
Grafana supports only basic authentication.
Sentry supports only basic authentication.

questions.question: What is required before using push connectors for event collection in Event Management?

options.text: The ITOM Visibility plugin must be activated
The Event Management Connectors plugin must be installed from the ServiceNow Store
A dedicated MID Server cluster must be configured
The Discovery plugin must be running

explanation.correct: Integrating with push connectors is only available by installing the Event Management Connector plugin from the ServiceNow Store. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/push-event-listener.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: ITOM Visibility is not required for push connectors.
A dedicated MID Server cluster is not required; some push connectors collect through the instance directly.
Discovery is not a prerequisite for push connectors.

questions.question: Which component runs the SNMP listener for collecting SNMP traps?

explanation.correct: The SNMP listener runs on the MID Server, which acts as a collection endpoint for SNMP traps. The MID Server sends the traps to the ServiceNow instance for further processing. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: The SNMP listener runs on the MID Server, not directly on the instance.
There is no SNMP Gateway appliance in ServiceNow architecture.
The Event Management plugin does not run the SNMP listener; the MID Server does.

questions.question: An organization needs to collect events from a monitoring tool that is not natively supported by Event Management. What approach should they take?

options.text: Wait for ServiceNow to release a native connector
Create a custom pull connector with a script, connector definition, and connector instance
Use the Discovery plugin to import events
Manually enter events through the ServiceNow UI

explanation.correct: You can create a customized pull connector that requires a script, connector definition, and connector instance to retrieve events on behalf of an event source. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Creating a custom connector is the recommended approach rather than waiting.
Discovery is for CI identification, not event collection.
Manual entry is not scalable; custom connectors automate collection.

questions.question: Which event collection method does NOT require a MID Server?

explanation.correct: The AWS push connector processes Amazon Web Services alarms with event collection through the instance directly, not requiring a MID Server. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/connectors-and-listeners.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: BMC TrueSight event collection is through the MID Server.
As the name implies, the Azure MID Push Connector collects through the MID Server.
The GCP MID Push Connector collects through the MID Server.

questions.question: What are the four methods by which Event Management can collect events sent to the instance?

options.text: Direct instance, MID Server, SNMP trap, and email
Direct instance, REST API, database query, and webhook
Pull connector, push connector, SOAP API, and syslog
MID Server, email, FTP, and SSH

explanation.correct: After event collection configuration, Event Management can collect events that are sent directly to the instance, or via the MID Server, SNMP trap, or email. Reference: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/xanadu-it-operations-management/page/product/event-management/concept/push-event-listener.html

wrongAnswers.explanation: Database query, REST API, and webhook are not the primary collection categories described in the documentation.
SOAP API, syslog, and FTP are not primary event collection methods for Event Management.
FTP and SSH are not event collection methods in Event Management.
